source_references: Decision Register DEC-014 Platform AI plus BYOK
Decision Register DEC-023 security minimum: secret handle
freeze_boundary: Draft only. Materializes exactly: the PT-010 requirement that a manifest sees a REFERENCE only and that revocation is immediate; the PT-010 and SEC-005 and SEC-012 requirement that no browser, log, event, job, analytics or error-trace surface sees plaintext; the INF-006 requirement that rotation carries an owner and a date; the SEC-009 requirement that a credential action records actor, reason and correlation; and the PT-010 managed/BYOK ownership split. NOT inferred and open before freeze: the credential storage and encryption mechanism (SEC-005), the resolver protocol and its scope check (PT-010), rotation OVERLAP semantics (whether a `rotating` handle still resolves is deliberately left unconstrained because no source states it), the revocation propagation mechanism, and the retention of a revoked handle. TWO OPEN CONFLICTS ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. (1) OWNERSHIP: CTR-MOD-001 `secret_handles` already fixed the pattern `^secret:[a-z0-9._-]+$`, but Decision Register 5.2 owns CTR-MOD-001 to A0 and CTR-SEC-001 to A0+A1, so a single-owner contract fixed the syntax of a jointly-owned one with no RFC. This contract ADOPTS that pattern as precedent, because two different handle syntaxes would stop the two contracts composing, and records the irregularity for the A1 owner to dispose of. This author must not resolve it. (2) THE PATTERN IS NOT A CONTROL: see x-opacity-limitation on `handle`. It excludes mixed-case base64 and nothing else, and the repository secret scanner detects only strings the pattern already rejects, so schema and scanner compose to zero coverage against a credential smuggled inside a conforming handle body. No rule was invented to make it look stronger. A1 must specify a handle ISSUANCE format before freeze.
untestable_by_fixture: PT-010 requires revocation to be IMMEDIATE and SEC-005 requires the secret to be encrypted, masked and rotated. Immediacy is a property of a resolver over time and encryption is a property of storage; neither is a property of a single document, so no fixture can demonstrate either. Likewise SEC-012 requires that a key never reaches analytics or an error trace: the `redaction` block records that a producer ASSERTS each surface is safe, and a fixture can show the assertion, but only a runtime redaction test over real log, event, job and trace output can show it is true. Decision Register 5.2 lists 'redaction tests' as a required freeze artifact and they do not exist yet.
untestable_by_schema: Two rules this contract states in prose and JSON Schema cannot express. (1) OPACITY: no shape rule can distinguish a reference from the credential it refers to, so `handle` cannot be constrained to exclude embedded credential material; demonstrated by examples/accepted-gap-structureless-handle-body.json. (2) SCOPE BINDING: JSON Schema cannot compare one property against another, so nothing here checks that the `scope` a document claims is the scope the registry recorded when the handle was issued; a document, or a CTR-MOD-001 manifest listing the same handle, may claim another tenant's scope and be accepted. Both belong to the PT-010 resolver and are NOT claimed as materialized.

accepted_gaps.examples/accepted-gap-classification-bel: SEC-003 in the Meta/Security/Ops baseline requires a Public/Internal/Confidential/Restricted matrix in which every token and API key is classified, but SEC-003 is an undelivered Phase 0 task: it names the four classes and has not yet assigned the class a credential handle carries. This contract therefore enumerates the four classes and pins none, so it accepts a managed provider credential declared merely `internal`, which the finished matrix would almost certainly forbid for a credential. The fixture exists so that gap is visible and executable rather than hidden behind a passing test. The contract owner A1, delivering SEC-003, must assign the class and this schema must then pin it before freeze.
accepted_gaps.examples/accepted-gap-structureless-hand: Decision Register 5.2 requires an opaque reference and PT-010 requires that a manifest sees a reference only, yet this contract accepts a handle whose body is an unstructured lowercase token carrying no issuer, namespace or scope, and therefore cannot tell a registry reference apart from credential material encoded into one. Independent security review demonstrated that the pattern excludes mixed-case base64 and nothing else, and that the repository secret scanner detects only strings the pattern already rejects, so the two controls compose to zero coverage for exactly this case. No shape rule available to JSON Schema closes it and none was invented. What closes it is a handle issuance format specified by the A1 co-owner: an issuer-assigned identifier a producer cannot mint from credential material. Unresolved and required before freeze.
